body.statement: There are universal constants \(c,C>0\) such that, with probability \(1-o(1)\) over \(G_n\), the capsule law satisfies \(p_{\mathrm{acc}}(G)\ge1-n^{-4}\), \[c\frac{k}{n}\le\min_{u\in\mathcal U}\pi_u\le\max_{u\in\mathcal U}\pi_u\le C\frac{k}{n},\qquad \|\Gamma_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le C\frac{n}{k}\le C\frac{(d+1)^2}{\log(d+2)}.\] The constants hold uniformly along every sequence satisfying \(d\to\infty\) and \(d=o(\sqrt n)\).
body.justification: This is the new stable-set exposure covariance kernel: diagonal-scale operator control for both arms and their cross-covariance.
body.gap: Li and Li control one arm under codegree restrictions, and the conflict-graph design controls a different kernel at order \(d^2\); neither proves the logarithmically smaller two-arm norm.
body.consumer: The bound supplies the attaining design needed to close the unrestricted random-regular full-GATE frontier.

obligation.what_is_open: Prove, uniformly for a typical simple random \(d\)-regular graph, that the covariance operator of the accepted, symmetrized reservoir pair has norm \(O(n/k)\), together with uniform two-sided inclusion probabilities and the stated single-trial acceptance tail.
obligation.obstruction: The diagonal and same-arm simple-random-sampling scales are \(n/k\), but the opposite-arm block contains the radius-two incompatibility matrix.  Its constant mode must be canceled by the compatible-pair probabilities.  Acceptance conditioning and the random denominator \(\binom{|F_G(A)|}{k}\) make that cancellation nonexact, and the frozen primitives contain no mixing, switching, or spectral estimate controlling the residual operator.  Treating the asserted kernel bound as a lemma would assume the theorem's novel crux.
obligation.attempted: I expanded the signed covariance blockwise, used fixed arm sizes to identify the constant-mode cancellation in the uniform idealization, and tested diagonal, Schur, and centered distance-two spectral bounds.  Diagonal control proves necessity of the \(n/k\) scale; Schur control leaves an \(O(d^2)\) term and therefore misses the required logarithmic improvement.
obligation.partial_result:
The signed kernel has the exact positive-semidefinite representation
\[
\Gamma_G=S\operatorname{Cov}((X_u/\pi_u)_{u\in\mathcal U}\mid G)S,
\]
and therefore
\[
\|\Gamma_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}\ge
\max_{u\in\mathcal U}\left(\pi_u^{-1}-1\right).
\]
Thus the asserted order \(n/k\) is the smallest possible order once \(\pi_u\asymp k/n\).  For an incompatible opposite-arm pair the unsigned normalized covariance equals \(-1\); after applying the contrast signs this contributes \(+1\).  Fixed arm sizes force cancellation of the constant cross-arm mode in the exactly uniform case, but proving that acceptance conditioning and the random set \(F_G(A)\) preserve this cancellation in operator norm requires a uniform switching or spectral estimate for the weighted compatible-pair kernel.  The elementary Schur bound controls it only at order \(d^2+n/k\), which is too large by the required factor \(\log(d+2)\).
